newsitem.title: QATAR: GCC slams Puerto Rico model for Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: GCC slams Puerto Rico model for Palestinians.

text.p: The six-nation Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) on Sunday rejected Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's suggestion for a Palestinian self-rule entity on the model of Puerto Rico or Andorra.

The political, economic and military alliance also urged the rightwing leader to implement peace deals signed with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) and revive talks with Syria and Lebanon, stalled since his election victory in May.

"The GCC states rejected Netanyahu's stand on the Palestinian self-determination issue," Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani told reporters at the end of a two-day meeting of GCC foreign ministers in Doha.
"They reaffirmed that Palestinians should have the right to self-determination on their national soil, and not under Israeli authority," he said.

Netanyahu was quoted by Israel's Haaretz newspaper on Friday as saying he was against "complete Palestinian sovereignty and unrestrained self-determination." He said he preferred a self-rule entity on the model of Puerto Rico or Andorra.
Puerto Rico is an autonomous commonwealth in association with the United States. Andorra is a tiny principality between France and Spain famed for its ski resorts.
A senior Palestinian official described Netanyahu's remarks as "arrogant" and "irrelevant".
The Palestinians have won limited autonomy in much of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank under a 1993 peace deal.

Netanyahu opposes trading land for peace. His government is locked in talks with the PLO on implementing a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron signed by the previous government.
Qatar and Oman are the only GCC states that have allowed Israel to set up trade missions. Oman has also opened a commercial office in Tel Aviv.
But both Gulf states have stopped short of full diplomatic ties pending resolution of all Arab-Israeli conflicts in line with a GCC resolution.
The GCC also includes Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates.
